texts.value: Secreted antioxidant enzyme that acts as the primary scavenger of superoxide radicals in the extracellular space, converting them to hydrogen peroxide and thereby protecting tissues from oxidative damage (PubMed:12933702, PubMed:15761197). Also preserves nitric oxide bioavailability by preventing the formation of harmful peroxynitrite (PubMed:12933702). Stored in intracellular pre-formed vesicles of macrophages and neutrophils and released upon stimulation by inflammatory mediators (PubMed:31326693)
Homotetramer (PubMed:19289127). Directly interacts with ATP7A; this interaction is copper-dependent and is required for SOD3 activity (PubMed:16371425)

99% of SOD3/EC-SOD is anchored to heparan sulfate proteoglycans in the tissue interstitium, and 1% is located in the vasculature in equilibrium between the plasma and the endothelium (PubMed:8546689). In macrophages and neutrophiles, extracellular SOD2 in endocytosed and stored in intracellular vesicles (PubMed:31326693)

Expressed in blood vessels, heart, lung, kidney and placenta. Major SOD isoenzyme in extracellular fluids such as plasma, lymph and synovial fluid (PubMed:7959763). Stored in macrophages intracellular compartments (PubMed:31326693)

The variant Gly-231 which is found in about 2.2% of individual displays a 10-fold increased plasma EC-SOD content due to reduced heparin-binding affinity and thus the impairment of its binding ability to endothelial cell surface
Belongs to the Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase family
